0.content: SillyBunny is a fork of the latest version of SillyTavern with a graphical shell for desktop and mobile, a Home page, in-chat agents and two chat modes: Roleplay (default) and Conversation. Top bar: Backend (model connections, presets, prompts, agents), Customize (appearance, extensions, interface, data, logs), Search, Mode, Home and Characters. Home is the landing page when no chat is open. Most SillyTavern behavior and data formats still apply. SillyBunny-specific bugs go to github.com/SillyBunnyTeam/SillyBunny/issues; bugs that also happen upstream go to SillyTavern.

1.content: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on large amounts of text. It generates text by repeatedly predicting the next token, so replies depend on the prompt it receives. SillyBunny does not contain a model: it builds a prompt from the chat, character card and settings and sends it to a model that runs elsewhere, either a cloud API or a local server. The connection is chosen under Backend ▸ Connections. The same model can behave very differently under different prompts or presets. LLMs can state false things confidently.

2.content: A provider is the company or server that runs a model; the API is how the app reaches it. In SillyBunny this area is Backend and its first tab is Connections; there is no "API tab". Under Backend ▸ Connections, the Backend Type toggle chooses Chat Completions, Text Completions or Other (NovelAI, AI Horde, KoboldAI Classic), and a Source picker selects the provider. Then enter the key or URL, press Connect and pick a model. The status stays "Not connected..." or "No connection..." until it works. Test Message sends a short real prompt to verify the link; the provider may bill for it. Upstream SillyTavern calls the first choice "API".

3.content: A model is one specific trained LLM served by a provider. Models differ in quality, speed, price, context size, whether they reason, tool support and strictness. The model list appears after pressing Connect; for endpoints with no list (some Custom endpoints), type the Model ID by hand. Some features depend on the model rather than the provider: the app shows "Supported by the current model" or "Unsupported by the current model" icons for function calling and inline media. The setting "Remember Sampling Settings per Model" (Backend ▸ Presets) lets sampler values follow the model.

4.content: An API key is a secret string that identifies the account making requests and is billed for them. Treat it like a password. Paste it in Backend ▸ Connections, in the key box for the chosen source. Pressing Connect with that box empty marks it and shows a "Missing key" notice. After Connect is pressed the box hides it ("For privacy reasons, your API key will be hidden after you click 'Connect'."); the key-icon button "Manage API keys" manages saved keys. Keys are stored server-side in secrets.json in the user's data folder, and are not returned unless allowKeysExposure is true in config.yaml (default false). Local servers often need no key. OpenRouter offers Authorize (OAuth) instead of pasting a key. Keys do not belong in chat messages or character cards.

5.content: The prompt is everything sent to the model for one reply: instructions, character card text, persona, triggered World Info, example dialogue, recent history and the latest message. The model has no other memory of the chat. To see what was sent: the Prompt button on a message opens Prompt Itemization (a token breakdown); the bundled Prompt Inspector extension (Inspect Prompts / Stop Inspecting, Chat Completion only); or the terminal and browser console. Chat Completion builds the prompt with the Prompt Manager (Backend ▸ Editor); Text Completion uses the Context, Instruct and System Prompt templates (Backend ▸ Presets and Backend ▸ Editor).

6.comment: A6 System prompt and Main Prompt
6.content: The system prompt is the general instruction block that tells the model its job and style, normally sent first. Chat Completion: the Main Prompt item in the Prompt Manager (Backend ▸ Editor). Text Completion: the System Prompt group, with an "Enable System Prompt" toggle. Post-History Instructions are sent last, after the chat history, and usually outrank earlier text; in Text Completion the System Prompt toggle must be on for them to apply. A character card's own system prompt and post-history instructions replace the preset's when "Prefer Char. Prompt" and "Prefer Char. Instructions" are on. Older text calls Post-History Instructions the jailbreak.

7.content: "Preset" means several things. A Chat Completion preset holds sampling values plus the Prompt Manager's prompt list, order and toggles, and is chosen under Backend ▸ Presets. A Text Completion preset holds sampler values only. System Prompt, Instruct, Context and Reasoning templates are saved separately. A preset changes how the model is instructed and sampled; a character card changes who is played. Linking switches: "Keep API/Model Linked to Preset", "Keep Sampling Settings Linked to Preset" (checked by default) and "Remember Sampling Settings per Model". They are in the drawer "Preset API/Sampler Linking" on Backend ▸ Presets, and each of the first two shows one line that describes the mode it is in: "Linked mode: …" when on, "Independent mode: …" when off. On the Backend ▸ Editor page the header of the prompt list shows the active preset, with an "Autosave off" or "Read-only" badge after the title when it applies, and built-in presets can be read-only.

8.content: A character card is a file (PNG with embedded JSON, or plain JSON) holding a character's name, description, personality, scenario, first message, example dialogue, optional alternate greetings and an optional embedded lorebook. SillyBunny writes PNG cards with both a V2 (chara) and a V3 (ccv3) chunk and reads ccv3 first. Name, description, personality and scenario are permanent: always sent in the prompt. The first message and example dialogue are not; example dialogue is dropped when the context fills. Large cards leave less room for chat history. Cards are managed from the Characters button; the editor sections are Essentials, Character Fields, Advanced Fields, Greetings and Metadata.

9.content: A persona is the user's own identity in the chat: a display name, avatar and optional description, separate from the AI's character card. The description is placed in the prompt according to its Position setting: None, In Story String / Prompt Manager (default), Top or Bottom of Author's Note, or In Chat @ Depth. Personas can be locked to a chat or to a character, or set as the default. Switching persona does not rewrite older messages. Personas are managed in the Persona tab of the Characters menu (tooltip "Manage User Persona/Personality").

10.content: World Info (a lorebook) is a set of entries inserted into the prompt only when their trigger keywords appear in recent chat, or when an entry is marked constant. That saves tokens compared with putting all lore on the card. It guides the model but guarantees nothing about the output. Only an entry's Content is sent to the model; titles and keys are not. Lorebooks can be global, attached to a character (the primary lorebook is exported inside the card), attached to a persona, or attached to a chat. The editor is the World Info tab of the Characters menu. Conversation mode also scans lorebooks, with some limits.

11.content: Models read and write tokens, not letters or words. In English a token is about 4 characters or three quarters of a word, so 100 tokens is roughly 75 words; counts vary by tokenizer and language. Everything sent counts: card, persona, lorebook text, system prompt, history, reply space and reasoning. Token counts in the app are estimates unless the tokenizer matches the model. Settings: Backend ▸ Formatting ▸ Tokenizer (default "Best match (recommended)") and Token Padding (Text Completion only). Hosted APIs bill per token. The top-bar title can show Context Size, the current total tokens.

12.comment: A12 Context window and Context Size
12.content: The context window is how many tokens a model can handle in one request, including its own reply. The model sets this limit. The app's own budget should stay at or below it: "Context Size (tokens)" for Chat Completion and "Context (tokens)" for Text Completion, under Backend ▸ Presets ▸ Generation Settings. The prompt budget is the context size minus the response length. When history does not fit, the oldest chat messages are left out first; nothing is summarised automatically unless a summary extension is used. "Unlocked Context Size" (OpenRouter, NanoGPT, LinkAPI) lets the slider exceed the model's reported limit. Conversation mode sends only the last 32 thread messages and keeps older context through its memory summary.

13.content: Temperature controls how random token choice is. Below 1.0 is more predictable, above 1.0 more varied, and 1.0 uses the model's original probabilities. Where: Backend ▸ Sampling ▸ group Sampling ▸ Temperature. Slider ranges: Chat Completion 0 to 2, Text Completion 0 to 5, NovelAI 0.1 to 2.5; providers may impose their own limits. Too high gives incoherent or off-character text; too low gives repetition. Change one sampler at a time.

14.content: Samplers are the rules that pick the next token from the model's probability list. They are in Backend ▸ Sampling, and which controls show depends on the connected API and source. Chat Completion shows only what the source supports as controls (Temperature and Top P on nearly all; Frequency and Presence Penalty on OpenAI-style sources; Top K, Repetition Penalty, Min P and Top A on some); the Text Completion samplers it has no setting for are listed as inactive rows marked "Unavailable". Text Completion exposes many more. Top K keeps the K most likely tokens; Top P keeps the smallest set whose probabilities add up to P; Min P drops tokens below a fraction of the top token's probability; Repetition Penalty discourages tokens already used. Good values depend on the model; presets carry recommended sets.

15.content: Chat Completion sends the prompt as a list of role-tagged messages (system, user, assistant), the format ChatGPT-style APIs use. It appears as Chat Completions in the Backend Type toggle, with a Source picker for the provider. It is not cloud-only: a local server can be reached through Custom (OpenAI-compatible), and many cloud sources also exist as Text Completion (OpenRouter, for example). The difference is the prompt format, not where the model runs. The prompt is built with the Prompt Manager (Backend ▸ Editor); instruct and context templates do not apply. Function calling, web search, inline media, reasoning toggles and Prompt Post-Processing exist only here. KoboldCpp is also a Chat Completion source of its own, where KoboldCpp builds the prompt with the model's own chat template. It has its own URL field and shares the KoboldCpp API key and URL history with the Text Completion KoboldCpp type. Connect shows the loaded model, and the "KoboldCpp Model" row and /kcpp-model work here too in admin mode. Its samplers are Temperature, Top P, Top K, Min P, Top A, Repetition Penalty, Presence Penalty and Seed, and it has Additional Parameters of its own for anything else KoboldCpp accepts.

16.content: Text Completion sends the whole prompt as one long text and the model continues it. It appears as Text Completions in the Backend Type toggle. Sources include KoboldCpp, llama.cpp, Ollama, Text Generation WebUI (oobabooga), TabbyAPI, vLLM and Aphrodite, and also hosted ones such as OpenRouter, TogetherAI, Featherless and Mancer (upstream calls this list "API Type"). It is not an older or legacy format and is not local-only. It exposes many more samplers. Instruct-tuned models need the matching Instruct Template and Context Template. Tool calling and image inlining are Chat Completion only. KoboldCpp can switch its loaded model from SillyBunny when it runs in admin mode (started with --admin and --admindir). Backend ▸ Connections then shows a "KoboldCpp Model" row that lists the model and config files of that folder, plus "Reload launch model" and "Unload model". Choosing an entry makes KoboldCpp load it, and SillyBunny reconnects when it is ready. The /kcpp-model slash command does the same. An admin password goes in the KoboldCpp API key field.

17.content: Chat Completion messages carry a role: system (instructions), user (the human or persona), assistant (the model) and tool (tool results). Providers differ: some newer OpenAI APIs call the top-priority role developer, and Anthropic's API takes system text in a separate field and accepts only user and assistant turns. To cope, the Custom source offers Prompt Post-Processing: None, Merge consecutive roles, Semi-strict (alternating roles), Strict (user first, alternating roles) and Single user message, with "with tools" and "no tools" variants. Other toggles: Squash system messages, Use system prompt, Continue prefill. Text Completion has no roles; the Instruct template's prefix and suffix fields simulate them.

18.content: Tool (function) calling lets the model ask the app to run a defined function with structured arguments, then continue using the result. It is Chat Completion only and opt-in: tick "Enable function calling", the switch of the group of that name under Backend ▸ Presets. "Tool Call Recurse Limit" (default 5 rounds) stops loops. An icon shows "Supported by the current model" or "Unsupported by the current model". It cannot be used with the Prompt Post-Processing "no tools" variants. Continue, impersonate and background generations cannot trigger tool calls. "Interleaved Thinking" (OpenRouter and Custom) chooses which earlier reasoning is resent during tool use. "Enable web search" is a separate, provider-side feature.

19.content: Reasoning models produce a chain of thought before the visible answer, which helps multi-step tasks but costs time and tokens. Reasoning tokens count toward the response limit and are billed as output even when hidden, so incomplete or empty replies can mean Max Response Length is too low. Chat Completion settings under Backend ▸ Presets, in Request Options and the groups after it: "Request model reasoning", "Reasoning Effort", "Auto-append visible reasoning tags" and "Interleaved Thinking". For most sources "Request model reasoning" only asks for reasoning to be returned; it does not decide whether the model reasons. Reasoning shows as collapsible blocks; Backend ▸ Formatting ▸ Reasoning controls parsing and display.

20.content: Cloud models run on a company's servers, use an API key and are usually billed per token. Local models run on the user's own machine through a server program: no per-use fee, but limited by RAM and VRAM. Local servers usable through Text Completion include KoboldCpp, llama.cpp, Ollama, Text Generation WebUI (oobabooga), TabbyAPI, vLLM, Aphrodite and Generic (OpenAI-compatible) such as LM Studio or LiteLLM. Start the server first, then connect to its URL. Set the context size in the server and match it in the app. From inside Docker use host.docker.internal instead of 127.0.0.1. The SillyTavern team does not support installing local backends. A local API has no external filter, but a model can still refuse.

21.content: OpenRouter gives one account, key and credit pool for models from many companies, and the Connections tab says "We recommend OpenRouter if you're unsure." It is a Chat Completion source and a Text Completion source; tool calling and image inlining work only through Chat Completion. Steps: Chat Completions, Source OpenRouter, Authorize (OAuth) or paste a key from openrouter.ai/keys, Connect, pick a model, optionally Test Message. OpenRouter controls include Allow fallback models, OpenRouter Model Sorting, Model Providers and a "View Remaining Credits" link. Providers behind one model can differ in speed, price, quantization and moderation; a 404 can appear when the selected providers cannot serve the model. Limits change, so check OpenRouter's pages.

22.comment: A22 Costs, rate limits and quotas
22.content: Hosted APIs charge per token, with different prices for input (prompt) and output (reply). Long chats resend the whole prompt every turn, so cost per message grows with context; reasoning tokens bill as output. Cost multipliers: Multiple swipes per generation, Enable web search, large lorebooks or cards, long reasoning, and agents that run extra generations. Test Message is a real paid request. Cost aid: the "Max prompt cost" row of Backend ▸ Presets ▸ Generation Settings (OpenRouter, Electron Hub, Chutes). Limit kinds: credit or spend limits, rate limits (HTTP 429) and context limits. Fixes: wait and retry, add credits, lower Max Response Length or Context Size, or try another model. Prices and free tiers change, so check the provider's page.

23.comment: A23 Max response length and streaming
23.content: Max response length caps the tokens generated per reply; it is not a target. Labels: "Max Response Length (tokens)" for Chat Completion and "Response (tokens)" for Text Completion, under Backend ▸ Presets ▸ Generation Settings. A reply cut off mid-sentence usually means the cap was hit; for reasoning models hidden thinking uses the same budget, so replies can come back short or empty. Raising it leaves less room for chat history. "Streaming" (one checkbox per API family) shows the reply bit by bit; when off, it appears all at once. It changes when the output appears, not the output. If a stream fails midway, the error can arrive inside the stream. In Conversation mode reply length is a separate setting, Max Reply Tokens.

24.content: Text Completion models just continue text. Instruct-tuned models expect a specific wrapper (ChatML, Llama 3, Alpaca or Mistral, for example). The Instruct Template supplies the wrappers, the Context Template (story string) lays out card, persona and world info, and the System Prompt fills the instruction slot. They are in Backend ▸ Presets and Backend ▸ Editor; enable with "Enable Instruct Mode". The template must match the model, usually stated on the model card; symptoms of a wrong one include the model writing the user's turn, repeating role labels or ignoring instructions. Stopping Strings are in Backend ▸ Formatting. Chat Completion does not use instruct templates.

25.content: A hallucination is a fluent, plausible statement that is false. It happens with every LLM; providers say it can be reduced but not removed. A model knows only its training data (which has a cutoff) plus what is in the prompt, so it may not know the app's interface, newer models, prices or rules. It cannot see the user's screen or verify settings: where its steps differ from what the app shows, the app is correct. Recall worsens as the context fills, so details far back can be missed. World Info helps but does not guarantee an entry's appearance. A character's backstory in roleplay is fiction by design. "Enable web search" is a provider-side option on some sources.

26.content: A refusal is either a model refusal or a provider filter. A model refusal arrives as a normal reply in which the model declines or hedges. A provider or API filter blocks the request or reply and returns an error or an empty result. For Google sources, SillyBunny sends Gemini's adjustable safety thresholds as off; blocked results are reported as "API returned no candidate" with "Prompt was blocked due to : <reason>", and Google's built-in protections still apply. According to SillyTavern docs, cloud APIs filter to varying degrees, OpenRouter enforces no moderation unless the model's vendor requires it, and local APIs have no external filter, though a model can still refuse. To tell them apart, check whether it is an error or blocked message or a normal reply that declines.

27.content: The top bar is always visible. Left to right: Backend, Customize, Search (magnifier), Quick Access buttons; the centre title; then extension buttons, Quick Access buttons, the Mode switcher, Home and Characters. Shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+U Backend, +I Customize, +F Search, +M Mode, +O Home, +P Characters. Clicking the centre title closes open overlays and returns to the chat without closing it; Home closes the chat. The title defaults to "SillyBunny" and is set in Customize ▸ Appearance ▸ "Top Bar Label": any of Context Size, Character Name and Custom Text, alone or together, joined with a middle dot (the same on every screen width; a label that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis). The desktop switch "Icons Only Top Bar" (Customize ▸ Interface ▸ Desktop) hides the button labels. On a narrow window the bar drops the labels by itself, then hides the title, and Quick Access buttons that still do not fit move into the Quick Access menu (the ⋮ button). Phones show icons only. On Home the Mode button shows the mode new chats will open in.

28.content: Backend ▸ Connections is the first Backend tab: "Configure the model backend for all AI character responses. We recommend OpenRouter if you're unsure." Groups: "Connection Profile" (all-in-one saved setups), "Backend" and "General". In Backend, the Backend Type toggle offers Chat Completions, Text Completions and Other (NovelAI, AI Horde, KoboldAI Classic), then a Source picker. Provider blocks have Connection (API key and test), Model, Providers and Advanced sections. Other labels: Status, "Auto-connect to Last Server", "View Hidden API Keys", "Custom Model", "Reveal API Key". A masked key field shows a "Caps Lock On" icon while it has focus and Caps Lock is on. Home ▸ Getting Started ▸ "Connect a Model" ▸ Show Me opens this tab. The Help icon here links to SillyTavern's connection profile docs. With the Custom (OpenAI-compatible) source, the "Custom Endpoint Profiles" expander holds "Endpoint Profiles": named sets of a URL, an API key, a model ID and the Additional Parameters (extra body fields, excluded body fields and headers, set with the "Additional Parameters" button in Advanced). Choosing a profile applies what it stores, and None clears the fields. An edit of the Additional Parameters is kept with the selected profile; "Save Custom Endpoint Profile" stores the current URL, key, model and parameters under the profile name, and "Delete Custom Endpoint Profile" removes the profile. A connection profile's own Additional Parameters still take priority over those of its endpoint profile.

29.content: Backend ▸ Sampling ("Modify model text parameters here - useful for dialing in responses!") shows only the section for the active API, titled Backend: Chat Completions, Text Completions, Kobold/Horde or NovelAI. Other APIs show "No unified samplers for this backend yet". Groups: Sampling, Penalties & Repetition, Advanced Algorithms, Token Control, Banned Tokens/Strings and Output & Generation. Each section notes "Some backends ignore samplers they do not support" Many samplers appear only for Text Completions. In the Chat Completions section a sampler that Chat Completions has no setting for stays in the list as an inactive row with the badge "Unavailable" and the note "Not available in Chat Completions. Custom endpoints can send it with Additional Parameters." The NovelAI section lists its sampler order under Output & Generation as "Samplers Order": a list that is locked at first (the lock button is titled "Unlock Sampler Reordering"; unlocked, its title is "Lock Sampler Reordering") and that can then be dragged to reorder, and each sampler in it has an on/off toggle that the keyboard reaches. Logit Bias is in the Token Control group. Chat Completions has a "Logit Bias Preset" select with new, import, export and delete buttons and an "Add bias entry" button; Text Completions shows a Logit Bias list for the backends that support it. Each entry is a row with a field for text or token IDs, a value from -100 to 100 and a remove button, and the rows can be dragged to reorder. Chat Completion presets also hold some sampler values, and the Presets tab has its own Sampling group. The tab links Geechan's sampling guide at rentry.org/samplersettings.

30.content: Backend ▸ Presets ("Manage presets, templates, and generation settings") shows groups that depend on the API. Chat Completions: Presets, Generation Settings, Sampling, Character Names Behavior, Continue Postfix, System Messages (formerly Character Names & Prompt Formatting, which the settings search still finds), Reply Prefill, Request Options and the groups after it for the settings that depend on one switch (Enable function calling, Send inline media, Request inline images, Request model reasoning, Auto-append visible reasoning tags), Prompt Caching (the switch Enable Prompt Caching, with Caching at Depth and Extended Cache TTL under it, for every Chat Completion source), then Reasoning Template. Prompt Caching and three rows of Request Options write to config.yaml: they save at once when changed, apply to new requests with no dialog and no restart, and show only for an admin. Adaptive Thinking (Claude and LinkAPI) follows Reasoning Effort, and API Version (AI Studio and LinkAPI) and Thought Signatures (AI Studio, Vertex AI, OpenRouter and LinkAPI) follow Verbosity. Enable Prompt Caching turns on the system prompt cache of both Claude and Gemini; turning it off also sets Caching at Depth to -1. A row whose value an environment variable sets is dimmed. Text Completions: Presets, Generation Settings, System Prompt, Instruct Template, Context Template, Character Names and Reasoning Template; NovelAI adds Phrase Repetition Penalty, Preamble and Banned Tokens before Reasoning Template; its sampler order is on Backend ▸ Sampling. The Reasoning row at the end of Reasoning Template opens Backend ▸ Formatting ▸ Reasoning. The "Edit prompts" button jumps to Backend ▸ Editor. Home ▸ Getting Started ▸ "Set Up a Preset" (Optional) opens this tab. Bundled Extras ▸ Presets lists "Geechan - Universal Roleplay (v5.2)" and "TLD Card Conversion Preset".

31.content: Backend ▸ Editor edits prompt content, order and placement, and depends on the connected API. For Chat Completion it shows the Prompt Manager (prompt list with toggles, reordering, editing and placement) and Utility Prompts (impersonation prompt, WI format, scenario format, personality format, group nudge, continue nudge and others). For Text Completion it shows System Prompt, Instruct Template and Context Template. The page starts with the prompt list, and the list header carries its context: the line under the title reads the active preset, the backend and the counts (for example "Default · Chat Completions · 11 active · 28 tokens"), an "Autosave off" or "Read-only" badge follows the title when it applies, and the Presets button before Search Prompts goes back to the Presets tab. A search replaces that line with its result count. Ctrl/Cmd+S saves. The Chat Completion prompt list header has the Presets button, Search Prompts, Add Prompt and Prompt List Actions (⋮). Prompt List Actions holds Import Prompt List, Export Prompt List, Select and Reset Order. The Sort button ends the search bar, which Search Prompts opens, and offers Prompt Order, Title A-Z, Title Z-A, Tokens ↗ and Tokens ↘; the choice is kept, and the button shows as pressed while the list is not in Prompt Order. A sort changes the view, never the order the prompts are sent in, so only Prompt Order lets the list be reordered: dragging, Move Up, Move Down and Alt+Up, Alt+Down, Alt+Home and Alt+End on a focused row are off under any other sort and during a search; the grip is for dragging with a pointer, and the keyboard moves a row from the row itself. Under another sort the list heading "Prompt Order" reads "Main Prompts", and a prompt with no token count yet stays after the counted ones. Select starts selection mode for the prompts of the order and the available ones, not the utility prompts or the Agents row, with the actions Turn On, Turn Off, Remove From List (a toast offers Undo) and Delete, which asks "Delete N prompts? This cannot be undone." A search with no match shows "No Results Found" with "Try a different search". The Text Completion view has no Sort, Add Prompt or Prompt List Actions. The Characters menu has a different tab also named Editor, for character cards and groups.

32.content: Backend ▸ Formatting ("Adjust token counting, stopping strings, text cleanup, and reasoning display") is also where the older Advanced Formatting button leads. Groups, in order: Tokenizer & Padding; Stopping Strings (text that stops generation, with optional macro replacement); Reply Prefix; Text Cleanup (line breaks, extra spaces and unfinished sentences in replies); Reasoning (how reasoning is parsed and displayed, with a Reasoning Template row that opens Backend ▸ Presets ▸ Reasoning Template); Add to Prompts (whether reasoning blocks are included in prompts, and how many); Rendering (keeps specified standalone text from being treated as Markdown); Advanced Formatting, the last group, with a Help link to the SillyTavern documentation page and the Master Import and Master Export rows (import or export all formatting settings in one file; shown for Text Completions, Kobold, NovelAI, Horde and Chat Completions text models, hidden for message-style Chat Completions). Regex is a separate extension, under Customize ▸ Extensions.

33.content: Backend ▸ Agents ("Configure your in-chat agents here. They can be configured for pre-gen, post-gen, or as a side companion.") is the in-chat agents list. The header has the "Agents On" master switch, Stop, Search Agents, "Add Agent" (New Agent, New Companion, New Agent From Template…, New Companion From Template…, AI Maker…, Import…) and "Agents Menu" (Settings, Companions Overview, Agent Groups, Select, Update All, Fix Trackers, Export All…). Sections: Pinned, Before Reply, Before and After Reply, After Reply and Companions. Each agent has an on/off switch and a menu with Pin to Top, Preview Prompt in Context, Run on Last Message, Duplicate, Export…, Restore Default… and Delete…. The Left Quick Access slot defaults to an Agents button.

34.content: Customize ("Personalize your workspace, add/remove extensions, modify server settings, or check logs here") has six tabs in this order: Appearance, Extensions, Interface, Messages, Data & Security, Logs. Appearance: themes (with a Custom CSS row and a reset), colors, layout, fonts, "Top Bar Label" and Quick Access Shortcuts. Extensions: install and manage extensions. Interface: General (splash character, Compact Mode), Desktop (including "Keep Characters Open", which keeps the Characters page open after a chat is picked; it applies above 768 px wide and is off by default), Mobile, Bottom Bar (bottom bar size, Show Bottom Chat Bar, Show Guided Generations Bar), Paper Texture, Typing (including markdown shortcuts), AutoComplete Settings, STscript Settings, MovingUI (when a saved panel position is outside the window, a banner says "A saved MovingUI panel position appears to be off-screen" and has a Reset Panels button), Miscellaneous. In Customize ▸ Interface ▸ Desktop, the switch "Limit Content Width" (on by default, above 768 px wide) keeps the contents of Settings pages and Window dialogs from stretching across very wide windows, and turning it off gives them the full width of the window. Messages: Sending, Chat History, Message Display, Swipes, Auto-swipe, Auto-Continue, Streaming, Smooth Streaming. Data & Security: General, Import & Restore, Export, App Status, Updates & Restart, Thumbnail Quality, Mobile Preset and config.yaml Editor. Logs: console logs for troubleshooting and bug reports. There is no "Server" tab; it became Data & Security. On a phone the page's tab list has its own Close button ("Close Settings"), and a tab opens its page with a Back button ("Back to Settings Navigation") to return to the list. Escape closes the Customize page, also while focus is still on its top-bar button. In Messages ▸ Message Display, "Markdown Engine" chooses how message text is rendered: markdown-it (the default, which follows CommonMark) or Showdown (the earlier renderer, kept as a fallback for chats, themes and extensions that depend on its output). The open chat is drawn again when the choice changes.

35.content: Global Search opens from the top-bar Search button, Ctrl/Cmd+F (skipped while a text field is focused) or a Quick Access slot set to Search. It searches every Backend and Customize control plus agents, characters, groups, World Info books (including entry contents) and personas; all query words must match. Results are grouped like "Backend · Sampling" and end with "Jump to setting"; clicking one opens the right tab and expands the control. ArrowUp/ArrowDown move, Enter opens, Escape clears and closes. No match shows "No Results Found" with "Could not find query. Try a broader term or a different setting name." Each settings page also has a sidebar search that filters its tab list; inside a list editor, Ctrl/Cmd+F focuses that list's own search.

36.content: Quick Access Shortcuts are icon-only top-bar buttons set in Customize ▸ Appearance ▸ Quick Access Shortcuts ("Assign a shell tab or universal search to each shortcut button in the top bar. Choose None to hide a button."). Six slots: Left, Right and Slot 3 to Slot 6 (Slot 3 (Desktop) and so on). The group is on the desktop settings page only, and the Quick Access buttons are hidden on a phone. Left defaults to Agents and Right to Extensions; None hides a button. Targets: Connections, Sampling, Presets, Editor, Formatting, Agents, World Info, Search, Settings (opens Customize), Extensions, Persona, Background.

37.content: The Characters button (Ctrl/Cmd+P) opens six tabs: Characters, Groups, Editor, World Info, Persona and Import. A search with no match shows "No Results Found" with "Try a different search" and a Clear All Filters button. The library header has Search, New and More…; Sort (with the List or Grid view) ends the search bar. More… holds Select, Manage Tags, Clear All Filters, Manage Folders and Import, and Search too when the header is too narrow for it. Select starts selection mode; Manage Tags opens the Tag Manager and Manage Folders the Folders window (both in the entry on the Tag and Folder Managers). Each row has Favorites, Duplicate, Convert to Persona and Delete, and the list ends in a Show More button while rows remain. The Import tab takes PNG, JSON, YAML, CHARX or BYAF files, or URLs ("Import From URL"), and results offer Chat, Edit and World Info buttons. The Editor tab has Essentials, Character Fields, Advanced Fields, Greetings and Metadata; its More… menu includes Set / Unset as Welcome Page Assistant and, while the card already has a linked lorebook, Link to World Info. It has no Convert to Persona (that is in the list's row menu and in Select), and for a card with no lorebook Link to World Info is in the editor's Related group instead. Home ▸ Getting Started ▸ "Get a Character Card" opens the Characters tab. With "Save External Media on Import" on (Customize ▸ Messages ▸ Character Handling; off by default), importing a card also downloads the images that the card links from other sites into the user's image folder and points the card at the local copies; a link that cannot be saved stays as it was. An exported card gets the original links back. A server's operator can forbid this for every user with allowExternalMediaImport in config.yaml.

38.content: Personas live in the Persona tab of the Characters menu ("Edit your own persona here for roleplay and chats!"). The list header has Search, New and a ⋮ menu named Persona Management with Global Settings, Select, Manage Folders, Backup, Restore and Usage Stats; the Sort button (A-Z or Z-A) ends the search bar, which Search opens. Rows offer Use This Persona, Duplicate and Delete in a menu, with Current Persona and Default Persona badges. With no personas the page offers a New button, and a search with no match shows "No Results Found" with "Try a different search", and the list ends in a Show More button while rows remain. Personas can be sorted into folders: Manage Folders in the list's Persona Management menu opens the Folders window, where folders are created, renamed, coloured, reordered and deleted and personas are added to or removed from a folder; the list shows each folder as a collapsible section with its persona count above the personas that are not in a folder; and Select in the same menu starts selection mode, where Move to Folder, Duplicate and Delete act on the chosen personas. A persona is in one folder at a time: the Folder row on its detail page ("No folder" by default) files it at once, without Save. Deleting a folder keeps its personas, and a duplicate stays in its source's folder. Global Settings include "Auto-lock a chosen persona to the chat". A persona's detail page has Identity, Persona Description, a "Persona Properties" row that shows the position (and depth and role for "In-chat @ Depth") and opens a window of that name where they are set, Scenario Notes, Connections (lock to the chat or to a character) and Lorebook ("Link to Persona Lorebook"). A persona with no name shows "Name required" under the name, and a scenario note with no label shows "Label required" under its label. Where the detail page opens as a pushed page with a Back button, Escape does what Back does. "Convert to Persona" turns a character into a persona; "Create Character Card From Persona" does the reverse. Persona switching is also in the bottom chat bar.

39.content: The World Info tab of the Characters menu ("Manage Lorebooks and World Information") is the lorebook editor; World Info is no longer under Backend. It has a book switcher (New, Import World Info), New Entry, Search and a book menu: Global Settings, Select, Rename, Duplicate, Export, Batch Import Embedded Lorebooks and Delete World Info. Global Settings include Scan Depth, Context %, Budget Cap, Min Activations, Recursive Scan and Insertion Strategy. Entry options include position (Before/After Char Defs, at Depth, Outlet and others), logic (AND ANY, AND ALL, NOT ALL, NOT ANY) and strategy (Normal, Constant, Vectorized). A character's primary lorebook is linked with Link to World Info in the character editor (in its Related group, or its More… menu once a lorebook is linked). In the entry editor, when the editor is narrow, the strategy, position and trigger chance collapse into one "World Info Properties" row that opens a window of that name. Apply Current Sorting as Order in the book menu asks for a Starting value and a Step, and shows a banner when some entries would be clamped to Order 0. In the Custom view and with no search, Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused entry one place, and Alt+Home and Alt+End to the first and last place; the grip is for dragging with a pointer. A search with no match shows "No Results Found" with "Try a different search". Importing a lorebook also saves the images that its entries link from other sites when "Save External Media on Import" is on (Customize ▸ Messages ▸ Character Handling), and an exported lorebook gets the original links back.

40.content: Home is the landing page shown when no chat is open; the Home button or Ctrl/Cmd+O closes the open chat to show it. The Main Menu (top right) has Display Mode (Full, Compact, List Only); Show Welcome, which opens the Welcome window; Recent Chats Settings, a dialog with "Max recent chats" and "Collapsed recent chats"; Show Getting Started (only while the tile is hidden and the display mode shows it); Preferences, which opens Customize; Keyboard Shortcuts; Help; and About SillyBunny. A Recent Chats list that fails to load shows "Chats Not Loaded" with Try Again. Quick Links tiles: Getting Started, Help and Bundled Extras. Getting Started has four steps: Connect a Model, Set Up a Preset (Optional), Get a Character Card and Start Chatting; each offers Show Me, Skip and Learn More. Once all are resolved, the tile shows a check and stays until Hide Getting Started in its window is used; Show Getting Started in the Main Menu brings it back. The Assistants section shows Reisen, Tewi and a third slot. Recent Chats has filter chips All, Individual, Groups and Conversation (one Tab stop; Left and Right move between them and choose the filter, Home and End jump to the first and last), and rows can be pinned, renamed or deleted. Home belongs to neither chat mode.

41.comment: A41 Help, About and Keyboard Shortcuts
41.content: F1 opens Help (also Home ▸ Help tile or Main Menu ▸ Help). Ctrl/Cmd+? or Main Menu ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts opens the Keyboard Shortcuts window, and so does the slash command /help hotkeys. General: Mod+O Home, Mod+U Backend, Mod+I Customize, Mod+P Characters, Mod+F Search, Mod+M Switch Mode (Mod is Ctrl, or ⌘ on Apple). Editors: Mod+S Save, Mod+F Find in List. Chat: Up Edit Last Message, Ctrl+Up Edit Last User Message, Left/Right Swipe, Enter Send, Ctrl+Enter Regenerate, Alt+Enter Continue, Escape Stop Generation, Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down Scroll to Context Line/Bottom. List Navigation (the same keys in every long list): Up and Down Previous Row and Next Row, Home and End First Row and Last Row, Page Up and Page Down Previous Page and Next Page, Left and Right Previous Card and Next Card (only where cards sit side by side, as in the Characters grid), Alt+Up and Alt+Down Move Row Up and Move Row Down, Alt+Home and Alt+End Move to Top and Move to Bottom (only in a list that can be reordered, and not during a search or under another sort). The window groups them under General, Editors and Lists, List Navigation, Chat and Formatting, and has a search (the toggle "Search Shortcuts"): a query matches a shortcut's name or its keys as written on this platform, so "cmd" or "ctrl" works, groups without a match hide, and no match at all shows "No Results Found". Formatting keys (Ctrl+B, I, U, K, and Ctrl+Shift+~ for Strikethrough) need "Markdown Hotkeys" on (Customize ▸ Interface ▸ Typing) and use Ctrl on every platform. Shell keys do not fire in a text field (Mod+M excepted). The tab list of a Backend, Customize or Characters page is one Tab stop: Up and Down move between the tabs (from the last to the first), Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space opens the tab that has focus. A long list is one Tab stop in the same way: Tab enters at the selected row, or the row that was last visited, reaches that row's own controls (such as Edit and the ⋮ button), and then leaves the list; the arrow keys move between rows, never into a row's controls, and skip hidden and filtered rows. Lists on settings pages keep every row in the Tab order. About SillyBunny (Main Menu) shows version, branch, commit and a debug-info box with Copy and Save, plus What's New, Website, Report an Issue, Troubleshooting, Credits and Legal (Fan Work, Art Licence, Third-Party Software).

42.content: Roleplay is the default chat mode ("Classic character-driven chat mode"). Chats are ordinary character or group chat files. The ☰ button beside the message box (tooltip and accessible name "Chat Actions", also the title of its sheet on a phone) opens the Options menu, which holds the full toolbox: Start new chat, Close chat, Manage chat files, Delete messages, Regenerate, Impersonate, Continue, Save checkpoint, Back to parent chat, Convert to group, Author's Note and more. Swipes, Continue, Impersonate, checkpoints, Temporary Chat, companions and Roleplay group chats exist only in Roleplay. World Info runs its full scan, including timed effects and every position. From Home, choosing Roleplay in the Mode switcher resumes the latest Roleplay chat, or opens the Characters panel if there is none.

43.content: Conversation ("Direct conversational AI mode") is a DM-style messenger workspace that replaces the chat area. It needs a character card. Threads are DMs kept in a separate Conversation store, not in chat files. Replies use their own prompt, in plain chat text without narration, and a character can answer in several bubbles. No swipes, Continue, Impersonate, checkpoints or Temporary Chat. Lorebooks apply: the speaking character's books, global books, the persona's book and the thread's "Lorebook Override"; the "Use Character Lorebooks" switch, when off, means replies use no lorebooks at all, the Lorebook Override included. Example-message and outlet positions are dropped and sticky or cooldown timers do not run. "Pals" is an older name for the conversations list.

44.content: The top-bar Mode button opens a menu with Roleplay and Conversation; its tooltip reads "Chat Mode: Roleplay (Ctrl+M)" or "Chat Mode: Conversation (Ctrl+M)". Ctrl+M (⌘M on Apple) toggles directly between the two and works even while typing. On Home neither mode is active, so the button shows the last used mode; picking Roleplay there resumes the latest Roleplay chat. Switching deletes nothing: closing Conversation only hides it, and history, branches, memories and schedules remain. Home assistant cards use the same memory: Start New Chat opens in the last mode and the card menu offers the other one.

45.content: Swipes are Roleplay only. Each message has left and right chevrons and a counter; Left and Right arrow swipe the last message when the input has no focus with text. Related message buttons: "Delete + Add Swipe" and "Jump to swipe history". Settings: "Multiple swipes per generation", "Swipe # for All Messages" and "Auto-swipe", which re-rolls automatically with "Minimum generated message length", "Blacklisted words" and "Blacklisted word count to swipe". Conversation mode has no swipes; its closest substitute is "Regenerate Message", which replaces the text and keeps no older version.

46.content: Roleplay: the Options menu item "Regenerate", Ctrl+Enter or /regenerate regenerates the last reply (in a group chat, the group reply). It is refused while the newest reply is being edited. Escape stops a generation. Conversation: "Regenerate Message" is a per-message action on character messages, shown in the expanded message pill or the message menu. It rebuilds the prompt from the messages before that reply, keeps the same speaker and overwrites the text in place, with no swipe history; the result is discarded if the thread changed meanwhile. "Force a Reply" is different: it asks the character to send a new message.

47.content: Roleplay: the pencil "Edit" button sits next to Copy, Delete and Message Actions. Edit mode offers Cancel, Confirm, Copy, "Add a reasoning block", "Move message up", "Move message down" and "Delete this message". Up edits the last message and Ctrl+Up the last user message when the input is empty and focused. Conversation: the pencil "Edit Conversation Message" appears only while the switch "Enable Quick-Edit DM Actions" is on (default on). "Character Prose Polisher" there adds a wand "Polish Character Message" to non-user messages. Other Conversation message actions: Reply, Copy Message, Pin Message, Branch From Here, Speak, Delete Message and reactions.

48.content: Continue is Roleplay only. It is in the Options menu ("Continue the last message"), on the composer arrow button, on Alt+Enter and as /continue. Settings: "Continue nudge", "Continue prefill", "Continue Postfix" and "Auto-Continue" with "Target length (tokens)": "Auto-Continue requests more text when a reply is shorter than this token count. Set to 0 to turn it off." Conversation mode has no continue action; new content comes from sending a message, "Force a Reply" or proactive and idle messages.

49.content: Impersonate is Roleplay only. The Options menu item "Impersonate" (tooltip "Ask AI to write your message for you"), the composer button and /impersonate make the AI write the user's message. The prompt used is editable as "Impersonation prompt". In-chat agents can opt in through the Impersonate generation type. Conversation mode has no impersonate; the user types their own DMs. The word "impersonate" is also a search alias of the Persona tab, so a search may surface Persona rather than the action.

50.content: Roleplay: Options ▸ "Delete messages" shows a checkbox on each message with Delete and Cancel (Escape cancels); /del also works. A single message has a trash "Delete" button, with the confirmation "Are you sure you want to delete this message?". Conversation: "Delete Message" works per message only, confirming "Delete this Conversation message?". Larger deletes are "Delete Branch…" and, in the Conversation menu, "Delete Conversation History…"; deleting a solo DM history also turns that character's Conversation off. Memory outlives deleted history until "Clear Memory" is used.

51.content: Roleplay has branches and checkpoints. Message buttons: "Create branch" and "Create checkpoint" (a flag button opens the checkpoint chat; Shift+click replaces it). Options: "Save checkpoint", "Back to parent chat", "Convert to group". A branch is a new chat file with the history up to that message, named "<chat name> - Branch #N". Temporary chats hide these controls. Conversation has branches only, no checkpoints: click the header title (tooltip "Branches") for the list, "New Branch…", "Rename Branch…" and "Delete Branch…". "Branch From Here" on a message copies the thread up to it, with the memory summary, into a new branch; "New Chat" in the Conversation menu adds a branch named "Chat N".

52.content: Temporary Chat (Roleplay only) is a Roleplay chat that is never written to disk. On Home each assistant card has a Temporary Chat button next to Start New Chat. A banner offers "Save as New Chat", which writes one normal chat file named "<character name> - <date/time>". The banner reads "This chat isn't being saved". Leaving after writing something asks "Keep this chat?" with Cancel, Discard or Save as New Chat; closing the browser tab warns once a message has been sent. Branch, checkpoint and Convert to group controls are hidden, and Vector storage skips it. From Conversation it opens in Roleplay. Separately, the slash command /tempchat opens a characterless temporary chat with "Assistant" that cannot be saved.

53.comment: A53 Chat files and Chat History
53.content: Roleplay chats are files. The Options item is "Manage chat files" and the chat-bar tooltip "View chat files"; both open the dialog titled "Chat History" (the slash command /chat-manager does the same). It lists saved chats, with a search field and a New Chat (+) button in its header. Each chat row has one ⋮ menu (titled "Chat Action") with Rename chat file, Export JSONL chat file, Download chat as plain text document and, last and in red, Delete chat file. The header's ⋮ "Menu" holds Import Chat, Backups, Label Current, Label Dated, Chat Cleanup and Help. A "Mass Delete Chats" window deletes chats older than a chosen age and protects the open chat. Also: Start new chat, Close chat, /delchat and /renamechat. Home's Recent Chats rows can be pinned, renamed and deleted. The Chat Archive extension adds a Chat Archive button to the Characters page; its Open Chat button opens the chat and closes the Characters page, as picking a chat from the list does, unless Customize ▸ Interface ▸ Desktop ▸ Keep Characters Open keeps it open (above 768 px wide). Conversation has no chat files: it uses branches, the conversations list and "Delete Conversation History…".

54.content: Roleplay and Conversation have separate group systems. Roleplay groups: Characters ▸ Groups tab ("Open and Manage Group Conversations"); the editor has Essentials, Members, Add Members, Chat Settings and Chat Overrides. "Group reply strategy": Manual, Natural order, List order, Pooled order. Generation handling: "Swap character cards" or "Join character cards" (exclude or include muted). Options ▸ "Convert to group" turns a solo chat into a group and cannot be reverted. Conversation group DMs: the conversations list "+" menu offers "New DM" or "New Group" and a group needs at least two characters. "@Name" mentions answer first; settings include "Allow Characters to Talk to Each Other" and "Character Chat Cooldown". Lorebooks are scanned per speaker. In a Roleplay group chat a speaker bar above the message box shows each enabled member as an avatar button. Pressing one selects who answers next and pressing it again clears the choice; Shift+click makes that member answer at once. Speak Now makes the selected member answer, with the notice "Pick a group member first" when none is selected, and Add New Greeting adds a greeting from the selected member. Hide Bar hides the bar, and "Show Group Bar" in the wand menu brings it back. The bar appears only while the open group has an enabled member, and it shows who is typing. The group editor's member menu also has Speak Now.

55.content: In-Chat Agents is a bundled extension managed in Backend ▸ Agents, with the master switch "Agents On". An agent is a stored prompt with a phase (before reply, after reply or both) and an execution (inline or companion); categories include Tracker, Randomizer, Content, Companion and Custom. Inline agents add a prompt to the main request or rewrite or append to the finished reply; companions make separate calls and store notes. Agents make extra model calls billed on the selected connection profile; Settings has "Default Connection Profile" and "Companion Connection Profile". "Fix Trackers" reruns tracker agents on the last reply. Agents are built for Roleplay chats; companion features are disabled in Conversation.

56.content: Bundled agent templates cover trackers, randomizers, content changers, companions and a tool (Pathfinder, hidden from the browser). Examples: Scene Tracker, Relationship Tracker, Time Tracker, Prose Polisher, Chaos Mode, Genre Randomiser. Use one with Add Agent ▸ "New Agent From Template…" or "New Companion From Template…". When a bundled version is newer, an agent shows "Update available" with "Update to v<n>" or "Update All (n)…". "Restore Default…" resets one agent to its template; "Reset Bundled Agents to Defaults" (Settings) resets all template-backed agents. Agents Menu ▸ "Agent Groups" lists Built-In Groups and Custom Groups, each with a Turn On button that installs missing agents and switches them on.

57.content: A companion is an agent with Companion execution: after the reply it makes a separate model call and stores a note, and does not replace the main reply. Bundled companion templates include Expressions Agent, Continuity Companion, Director's Commentary, Lorebook Scout, Memory Shard, Plot Compass, Chatroom, Chat Only and Message Inbox (the last three are Roleplay-side feeds, unrelated to Conversation mode). Notes appear in the Companion Panel (handle titled "Open the Companion Panel"), a side panel that docks beside the chat and becomes a sheet above the composer on a narrow window, as note cards on messages and on the Companions Overview page (Agents Menu). The Companion Panel is the tracker panel: the grip on a section opens a menu with Move Up and Move Down (an item that cannot apply is left out), and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move a focused section. Companions are Roleplay only: in Conversation the Overview shows "Companions Unavailable" and the panel is hidden.

58.comment: A58 Extensions: first and third party, installing
58.content: Extensions are in Customize ▸ Extensions. The first group at the top has no title and holds two rows with an arrow, "Manage extensions" and "Install extension" ("Import Extension From Git Repo"), and the switch "Notify on extension updates", which shows a notice when updates are available for supported third-party extensions. Under it, "Download Extensions & Assets" loads an asset list from the "Assets URL" field, and "System Extensions" and "User-Installed Extensions" list each extension as a row that opens its settings. Install asks for a Git URL and an optional "Branch or tag name (optional)"; only http and https URLs work. Buttons: "Install just for me" (admins; non-admins see Install) and admin-only "Install for all users". Repositories under github.com/SillyTavern or github.com/SillyBunnyTeam count as first party; any other URL shows "Install a third-party extension?". Install is a shallow git clone and fails with "Directory already exists" if the folder exists. Manage extensions lists built-in and installed extensions. Enabling or disabling an extension reloads the page.

59.content: Bundled Extras is a Home tile and window with the groups First-Party Extensions, Third-Party Extensions, Themes and Presets, plus a UI Themes row that jumps to Customize ▸ Appearance. First-party items (SillyBunnyTeam repositories) include CSS Snippets, Prompting Lab, Time Machine and World Info Lab. Third-party: Dialogue Colors, Summary Sharder, Group Chat Overhaul, LALib. Group Chat Overhaul includes Group Greetings, Group Utilities and Group SendAs, so turn off standalone copies of those before enabling it, or their controls appear twice. Themes: Moonlit Echoes, Terminal UI. Presets: "Geechan - Universal Roleplay (v5.2)" and "TLD Card Conversion Preset". Row states are Not installed, Installed and Enabled, with actions Install, Enable, Disable, Remove, Restore and Apply. Install uses the normal extension flow for the current user only, so third-party items show the third-party warning.

60.content: Character Expressions is a built-in extension (Customize ▸ Extensions) that shows sprites matching the emotions in messages. Its settings page (Customize ▸ Extensions ▸ Character Expressions) has a "Classifier API" select ([ None ], Local, Extras, Main API, WebLLM Extension and In-Chat Agent) and "Sprite Folder Override". Sprite files go in <user data>/characters/<character name>/ named [expression_label].[image_format]; several per expression need "Allow Multiple Sprites per Expression". Buttons include "Generate Missing Sprites", "Upload Character Sheet", "Redo Crop/Cleanup", "Stop Generation", "Upload Sprite Pack (ZIP)", "Remove All Sprites" and "Remove All Image Overrides". SillyBunny adds "Auto-Generate Missing Sprites During Chat", which uses the In-Chat Agent classifier, the bundled Expressions Agent companion and Quick Image Gen; next to it are "Share Quick Image Gen LLM Override Profile", "Sprite Generation Mode" (Separate images or Character sheet (auto-split)), "Sprite Framing" (Bust portrait or Full body) and "Remove Background (White/Solid-Color Sheets Only)". Customize ▸ Interface has "Visual Novel Mode". In the Echo, Whisper and Ripple chat styles (Customize ▸ Appearance, "Chat Style"), a character's message shows the character's current expression sprite in the large picture slot instead of the profile picture, as long as the character's sprite folder has a sprite for a label of the expression list. The slot takes the current expression, then the fallback expression, then neutral, and keeps the profile picture when none of them has a sprite. The small round avatar beside the name stays the profile picture, and user, system and narrator messages are unchanged. No setting turns it on or off. The sprite code is built on the Roleplay chat surface; Conversation support is not confirmed.

61.content: Quick Image Gen is a built-in extension ("Generate images from prompts or chat scenes, with style presets and a gallery."). Its drawer has Generate, "Quick Setup" (pick a provider, paste a key, choose a style), a gallery. Providers include Pollinations, NovelAI, GPT Image (OpenAI), Local (A1111/ComfyUI) and Custom API. Each message has a palette button to generate an image from it. Slash commands: /qig, /qig-auto, /qig-cancel. API keys are stored in the extension's own settings rather than secrets.json. Expressions auto-sprites and Conversation selfies ("Selfies Through Quick Image Gen ([selfie])") use it; Conversation uses Image Generation instead when that is configured. Image Generation is a different built-in extension. Both Image Generation and Quick Image Gen include NovelAI "Precise Reference" for NovelAI V4.5 models (not V5): up to 16 reference images with Character, Style, or Character & Style modes and independent Strength and Fidelity controls, costing 5 additional Anlas per reference per image (blocked in Image Generation when "Avoid spending Anlas" is on).

62.content: Dialogue Colors is a third-party extension, listed in Bundled Extras ▸ Third-Party Extensions and not part of the repository; installing it shows the third-party warning. Per its own README it colors dialogue and thoughts with an LLM engine (the model writes color tags, which persist) or a Local DOM-only engine (render-only and reversible), with storage scopes Per chat, Per card or Global. It opens from "Dialogue Colors" in the Extensions panel. Local colors vanish on refresh by design. It is third-party software that may change, and SillyBunny does not support it. It is built for the Roleplay chat; Conversation use is not confirmed.

63.comment: A63 Themes, Custom CSS and CSS Snippets
63.content: UI themes are set in Customize ▸ Appearance with the "UI Theme" select and its ⋮ menu to update, save, import, export and delete a theme file. Bundled themes include Libadwaita Dark, Libadwaita Light, Catppuccin, Dracula, Nord and Gruvbox. The UI Theme group also has Accent Colors (buttons such as "Blue Accent"; the one that matches the current accent shows as pressed), a "Custom CSS" row and a "Reset Theme to Default Libadwaita Dark" row, and "Custom RGB Accent" is a group of its own with a switch and Primary and Secondary Accent colors. "Chat Style" options are Flat, Bubbles, Document and Echo. The "Font Settings" group has one "Preset" select with Default (none), five bundled presets (Inter, JetBrains Mono, Roboto, Public Sans and Source Serif 4) and any imported fonts. Its ⋮ menu, Font Actions, has Import Font and, in a last section while an imported font is selected, Remove Font. Import Font takes .woff2, .woff, .ttf and .otf files of up to 5 MB each, up to 20 files in all, and stores them on the SillyBunny server. At most 20 font families can be imported: a file for an extra family is skipped and the other files go on. A font collection, an empty file, a file whose contents do not match its extension and a font the browser cannot load are refused. When a file does not name its family, a dialog asks for the Family, the Weight and the Style (Upright or Italic). Remove Font asks first, then deletes every file of that family from the server, and the font returns to Default if it was selected. Presets and imported fonts load from SillyBunny, not from Google. A Google Fonts name saved by an older version stays applied and is listed under "Google Fonts" until another font is chosen. The "Custom CSS" row opens a Window with a full-height monospace editor that styles the whole interface. The Window's header bar holds the save state, which saves the CSS into the current theme, and the "Generate CSS With AI" wand, which uses a chosen connection profile. "Reset Theme to Default Libadwaita Dark" asks "Reset Theme?" ("Theme settings and custom CSS will be wiped. This is irreversible!") with Cancel and Reset. Reset restores the Libadwaita Dark theme that SillyBunny ships (its ten colors, the background and chat field blur and background effects, Blur Strength, Shadow Width and the default font), clears Custom CSS and selects Libadwaita Dark. Layout, Chat Display, the visual switches and backgrounds stay as they are, and imported fonts stay installed. CSS Snippets (a first-party extension in Bundled Extras) manages snippets that can be global, per theme or per chat. Moonlit Echoes and Terminal UI are theme extensions, installed like any extension. Themes and Custom CSS apply to both modes; Conversation has its own stylesheet.

64.content: Customize ▸ Data & Security ▸ Export has a "Download Backup" row ("Download a complete backup of your user data.") and "Settings Snapshots". It downloads a ZIP of the user's data folder, named <handle>-<timestamp>.zip. secrets.json is left out unless allowKeysExposure is true, so API keys saved in Connections are not in the ZIP, and the toast "Secrets Not Included" appears. Automatic backups go to the user's backups folder; chat backups are on by default and settings backups feed the Settings Snapshots list. In the "Chat History" dialog, the Backups button lists chat backups to download, import or delete. Before updating, back up the data folder (the whole data folder in multi-user setups).

65.content: Customize ▸ Data & Security ▸ "Import & Restore" imports a SillyTavern setup. Options: the "Import From Folder Path" field (the SillyTavern install, its data folder or one user folder; button Import Folder), the button "Sync Extensions" (third-party extensions only, with a report) and "Import From Backup ZIP" (the ZIP SillyTavern exports; button Import Backup ZIP). Files with the same name are replaced and the page reloads. Imports go into the logged-in account, so in multi-user mode log in as the target user first. In multi-user mode only admin accounts see "Import From Folder Path" and "Sync Extensions"; other accounts see only "Import From Backup ZIP". The error "Multiple SillyTavern user folders were found" means the exact user folder must be given. SillyBunny keeps upstream data formats. Conversation threads are SillyBunny-only and do not come from SillyTavern.

66.comment: A66 Data folder, accounts and secrets
66.content: User data is under dataRoot (default ./data), in one folder per user; single-user mode uses default-user. The --global flag uses OS app-data paths instead. Docker maps ./docker/data. Multi-user accounts are off by default (enableUserAccounts: false in config.yaml, editable in Customize ▸ Data & Security ▸ config.yaml Editor; restart after). With accounts on, Data & Security shows Account, Admin Panel (admins only) and Logout. API keys entered in Connections go to secrets.json in the user's folder; the field is blank after saving, and reading values back needs allowKeysExposure: true (default false). By default the server does not listen on the network (listen: false) and uses a whitelist (whitelistMode: true).

67.content: Supported installs are a git checkout (bootstrap installer or git clone) and Docker; ZIP installs are unsupported from v2.0.0. Git update options: (1) in app, Customize ▸ Data & Security ▸ Updates & Restart, with "Check for Updates", "Update & Restart", "Restart Server" and "Auto-Stash Local Changes Before Pulling" (admin only; fast-forward only); (2) the ./start.sh launcher checks on each launch (SILLYBUNNY_AUTO_UPDATE=0 disables it); (3) manually with git pull --ff-only, then bun install if dependencies changed. Back up the data folder first. Local changes or a diverged branch block updates. Docker: pull the new image and recreate the container. A copy not installed with Git shows "Reinstall with the installer to get updates".

key: nothing happens when i press enter
68.content: Likely causes in order: (1) Not connected. Pressing Send shows a "Not connected to API!" notice whose "Show Me" button opens Connections; the message stays in the box, and slash commands still run. Fix: Backend ▸ Connections, press Connect and wait for "Valid". (2) A generation is still running; use Stop ("Abort request"). (3) A message is being edited: "You cannot send a message during a swipe-edit." (4) Customize ▸ Messages ▸ Sending ▸ "Enter to Send:" Disabled, Automatic (PC) or Enabled; on phones Automatic does not send on Enter. (5) With "\"Send\" to Continue" on, Send with an empty box continues the last message. (6) "ST Server cannot be reached": the server stopped or is blocked. (7) Conversation: "Pick a DM first".

69.content: The error toast shows the provider's own message, under titles such as "Chat Completion API", "Text Completion API" and "Text generation error". For a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 5xx it adds one line on what to try: for 401 or 403, check the API key in Backend ▸ Connections; for 404, check the model and address there; for 429, wait or check your credits with the provider; for 5xx, try again in a few minutes. When the provider sent no text, the toast shows the HTTP reason phrase (for example "Unauthorized"); the full provider text is also in Customize ▸ Logs. A 401 may appear as 400. General meanings: 401 or 403, a bad, missing or expired key, wrong permissions or a region or IP block; 404, a wrong Custom endpoint URL, missing /v1 or an unavailable model; 429, a rate limit or no credits; 5xx or 502, the provider is down or unreachable. Test Message is the best first check. A 403 "Forbidden" page can come from SillyBunny's own IP whitelist.

70.content: Settings: "Context Size (tokens)" and "Max Response Length (tokens)" for Chat Completion, "Context (tokens)" and "Response (tokens)" for Text Completion. The toast "Mandatory prompts exceed the context size." means the fixed prompts do not fit: raise the token limit or disable custom prompts. "Pre-generation intercepts exceed the context size" comes from pre-generation agents. A provider-side overflow (HTTP 400) shows the provider's own message in the error toast; the full text is also in Customize ▸ Logs. Remedies: raise Context Size to the model's real window, lower Max Response Length, trim the card, disable large World Info entries or agents that add prompt text. Conversation mode sends only the last 32 messages, caps card text, and has its own "Max Reply Tokens" setting.

71.comment: A71 Troubleshooting: empty or cut-off replies
71.content: Empty after thinking: the warning "The model finished reasoning but returned no reply text" means a reasoning model spent its budget thinking; raise Max Response Length (tokens), lower Reasoning Effort or turn off Request model reasoning. Cut off mid-sentence usually means the Max Response Length cap was hit; it is under Backend ▸ Presets ▸ Generation Settings and is 300 tokens by default for Chat Completion (350 for Text Completion). A reasoning model's hidden thinking counts against the same cap and can use more than 300 tokens before any reply text, so it needs a cap well above the default. "Trim Incomplete Sentences" can remove a dangling end, except when the cap was reached. Fixes: raise the cap, use Continue (Roleplay only), or enable Auto-Continue (Customize ▸ Messages ▸ Auto-Continue). A toast titled "Chat Completion API" or "Text Completion API" mid-stream is an upstream error. In Conversation, reply length is "Max Reply Tokens" in the thread's Conversation settings (16000 by default), and newlines split a reply into several bubbles.

72.content: Controls are in Backend ▸ Sampling, group "Penalties & Repetition" ("Control how the AI reuses tokens and repeats phrases"): Frequency Penalty, Presence Penalty and Repetition Penalty for Chat Completion, plus Repetition Penalty and DRY Repetition Penalty for Text Completion; which show depends on the connected API. General guidance: raise temperature a little, add small frequency or presence penalties, enable DRY where available. In the app: Auto-swipe (Customize ▸ Messages) can reject and regenerate replies by criteria including "Blacklisted words"; swipe or regenerate manually; edit repeated lines out of recent messages, since the model copies its own history; long first messages and example dialogue can seed loops.

73.comment: A73 Troubleshooting: the model ignores the card
73.content: First check what is actually sent: the bundled Prompt Inspector (button "Inspect Prompts") or the message's Prompt button (Prompt Itemization). In Chat Completion the Prompt Manager has a "Char Description" entry; if a preset disables or removes the card entries, the card is not sent (Backend ▸ Editor). "Prefer Char. Prompt" and "Prefer Char. Instructions" make the card's own prompts replace the preset's. A small Context Size trims history first, and long chats can drown the card. Agents may inject competing text. Conversation mode builds its own prompt with only the character description, personality and scenario (each truncated), plus the Conversation system prompt, so the Roleplay preset, first message and example dialogue do not apply.

74.content: First separate provider latency from app slowness; the server console is under Customize ▸ Logs, and the "Message Timer" setting shows generation time. Longer Max Response Length and bigger Context Size are slower; streaming options are in Customize ▸ Messages ▸ Streaming. Agents add model calls before and after the main reply, so many agents or a slow agent model means long waits; disable them or give them a faster profile. Reasoning (Request model reasoning, Reasoning Effort) slows thinking models. On phones, Customize ▸ Messages has "iOS Streaming Stability" and "Android Streaming Stability" toggles. Conversation mode also makes background calls for memory summaries, auto-messages and selfies.

75.comment: A75 iOS loading failure and the boot guard
75.content: On iOS WebKit, a startup failure or timeout shows the full-screen panel "SillyBunny could not finish loading", explaining that stale cached files or blocked storage stopped startup. Buttons: "Clear Frontend Cache and Reload" (deletes Cache Storage and unregisters service workers) and "Continue Anyway"; "Startup Error Details" shows the captured error. If it repeats, clear the site's website data in the browser. Failures from third-party extensions do not trigger the panel. On other platforms the toast "Startup error" ("SillyBunny couldn't finish starting. Please refresh the page.") appears. About SillyBunny ▸ Troubleshooting has a debug-info box with Copy and Save for bug reports.

76.content: Differences confirmed in the code: a graphical shell replaces upstream's drawer top bar; settings are full-screen pages with a tab sidebar; Backend is reorganised into Connections, Sampling, Presets, Editor, Formatting and Agents, with the Prompt Manager in Editor; two chat modes, Roleplay and Conversation; in-chat agents with a Backend ▸ Agents tab; rebuilt character, persona, World Info and prompt editors; Bun runtime with a Node.js fallback; an "Import & Restore" group for SillyTavern setups in Customize ▸ Data & Security. SillyBunny aims to stay backwards compatible with upstream data, though extension compatibility "isn't guaranteed". Installs are a git checkout or Docker; ZIP installs are unsupported.

77.content: Reisen and Tewi are SillyBunny's built-in assistants. They appear as cards in the Home Assistants section, with a third slot. Until a choice is made, the third card is "Choose Assistant" and opens a window listing the library's other characters, so any character card can become the third assistant. A chosen character gets its own card, with "Choose Another Assistant…" and "Remove Assistant" in its menu. Each card has Start New Chat, Temporary Chat and an Assistant Menu offering a new chat in the other mode. Start New Chat opens in the last used mode; Temporary Chat is Roleplay only. While no model is connected, each card that can open a chat also shows a "Connect a Model" link under its subtitle, which opens Backend ▸ Connections; pressing the card itself still starts a chat. A missing bundled card shows a Restore button. If an edited bundled card has a newer bundled version, the menu shows "Update Available" (Keep Mine or Update).

78.content: Reisen Udongein Inaba ("Assistant Reisen" in the character list; everyone at Eientei calls her Udonge) is SillyBunny's main built-in assistant. Her card is the first in the Home Assistants section and offers help with setup and troubleshooting; she is the default Welcome Page Assistant and the voice of Getting Started. In Touhou Project she is a former Moon rabbit soldier who deserted the Lunar Defense Corps and now calls herself an Earth rabbit of Gensokyo. She lives at Eientei, in the Bamboo Forest of the Lost, as the disciple of Eirin Yagokoro, whom she calls Master, and the pet of Kaguya Houraisan. She is Eirin's pharmacy apprentice and the test subject for her new medicines, sells Eirin's medicine in the Human Village, and looks after Eientei's festivals and rabbits. Her ability is the manipulation of wavelengths. She became an assistant on Eirin's orders: SillyBunny reached Eientei as an artifact from the Outside World, Kaguya passed it to Eirin, and Eirin told Reisen to learn from the humans on the other side and guide them through the program. She is hard-working, overworked and easily flustered, and gives users plain, direct, step-by-step answers. Tewi Inaba, the second assistant, is her best friend and her constant prankster; nominally under Reisen, she ignores Reisen's orders. When Tewi joined, Reisen made her promise never to tell users a single lie.

79.content: Tewi Inaba ("Assistant Tewi" in the character list) is SillyBunny's second built-in assistant. Her card is the second in the Home Assistants section and offers help to users who are down on their luck. In Touhou Project she is an ancient youkai Earth rabbit, one of the longest-lived youkai in Gensokyo, who lived in the Bamboo Forest of the Lost long before Eientei was there. She leads the Earth rabbits, who obey only her, and keeps humans away from the forest and Eientei under a deal with Eirin Yagokoro, who in return shares her knowledge with the rabbits. Known as the Rabbit of Good Fortune, she can grant humans good luck, and she is famous across Gensokyo as a trickster with a taste for pranks, deals and new fashions. She was not assigned to SillyBunny: after Eirin gave the program to Reisen, Tewi took an interest in the "fashionable new program" and joined as the second assistant. Reisen made her promise never to tell users a single lie, and she keeps it: what she tells users is true, but she likes to give hints, leading questions and "lucky tips" so that users work out the last step themselves, and she answers plainly when a user is truly stuck. Reisen Udongein Inaba is her best friend and her favourite prank target; Tewi dodges chores and Reisen's orders, yet looks out for her like a big sister.

key: file a background in a folder
80.content: Backgrounds are picked in Customize ▸ Appearance ▸ Background, in a gallery with a Global tab and a Chat tab. A click or tap on a thumbnail sets it as the background. The Search field filters the gallery and the Sort button beside it changes the order. Under the tabs are Add Background, two zoom buttons that make the thumbnails smaller or larger, and a ⋮ menu with Select, Manage Folders and Auto-Select. In the Global tab a background can be in a folder. Each folder is a section with its name and a count, that opens and closes, and the backgrounds in no folder follow under the heading "No Folder". A background is in one folder: "Move to Folder" in its menu files it there, and "No Folder" takes it out. The menu of a background (Set as Background, Lock, Rename, Move to Folder, Delete) opens from the ⋮ button in the thumbnail's corner when the pointer is over it, with a long press on a touch screen, or with Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a focused thumbnail. Select, in the ⋮ menu, picks several backgrounds to move to a folder or delete; Delete asks first and says how many. Manage Folders creates, renames, recolours, reorders and deletes folders, and deleting a folder keeps its backgrounds. The Chat tab has no folders. While the Bunny Preset Tools extension is enabled, Customize ▸ Appearance also has an "Animated Backgrounds" group above the gallery: a "Video URL" field (a YouTube or direct video address) with a Use URL button, and the switches "Enable video and YouTube backgrounds", Muted, Loop and Autoplay and a Volume slider; the normal Add Background upload takes local MP4 or WebM files.

81.comment: A81 Selection mode, Sort and Show More
81.content: Several lists share three features. Selection mode acts on many rows at once. It starts from the Select item in the list's menu, by a right-click on a row, or by a long press on a touch screen (a press of half a second).
